scheme_name: Subsidy Scheme On Establishment Of 25 R.I.R. Birds’ Unit For Scheduled Caste
description:
The Subsidy Scheme on Establishment of 25 R.I.R. Birds’ Unit for Scheduled Caste was launched by the Government of India to promote poultry farming among Scheduled Caste communities.

This initiative aims to enhance the livelihood opportunities for Scheduled Caste families by providing them with the means to establish poultry units.

The scheme was introduced in the year 2019 as part of the broader efforts to empower marginalized communities in India.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to Scheduled Caste individuals to set up a poultry unit consisting of 25 Rhode Island Red (R.I.R.) birds.

The specific goal is to improve the income levels of beneficiaries through poultry farming, which is a sustainable source of livelihood.

Under this scheme, the government provides a subsidy of 50 percent of the total cost incurred in establishing the unit.

The maximum subsidy amount available under this scheme is ₹25,000 for each beneficiary.

This means that if the total cost of establishing the poultry unit is ₹50,000, the government will provide ₹25,000 as a subsidy.

The remaining ₹25,000 must be borne by the beneficiary.

To qualify for this scheme, applicants must belong to the Scheduled Caste category as defined by the Government of India.

There is no specific age limit for eligibility, but applicants must be adults and capable of managing the poultry unit.

Additionally, applicants must have a valid certificate confirming their Scheduled Caste status.

The scheme is open to both men and women from Scheduled Caste communities.

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme.

The application process for the Subsidy Scheme on Establishment of 25 R.I.R. Birds’ Unit involves several steps.

Interested beneficiaries must first approach the local Animal Husbandry Department or the relevant government office in their district.

They need to obtain the application form which is available at these offices or can be downloaded from the official government website.

The completed application form must be submitted along with the required documents.

Required documents typically include proof of Scheduled Caste status, identity proof, address proof, and a bank account statement.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the officials of the Animal Husbandry Department.

If the application is approved, the beneficiary will receive a sanction order detailing the subsidy amount.

The beneficiary must then establish the poultry unit as per the guidelines provided by the department.

After the establishment of the unit, the beneficiary must submit proof of the setup along with the expenditure incurred.

Upon verification, the subsidy amount will be disbursed to the beneficiary's bank account.

The timeline for the entire process from application to disbursement can vary but generally takes about 2 to 3 months.

The frequency of application is not restricted, and beneficiaries can apply for the scheme as long as they meet the eligibility criteria.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India.

The contact details for the Department can be found on their official website.

This scheme is part of a larger initiative to promote self-employment and entrepreneurship among marginalized communities.

The government aims to establish a significant number of poultry units across the country under this scheme.

As of the latest reports, the government has set a target to establish over 10,000 poultry units under this scheme in the first phase.

The scheme also aims to provide training and support to beneficiaries in poultry management and biosecurity measures.

This training is crucial for ensuring the success of the poultry units and enhancing productivity.

The Rhode Island Red breed is chosen for its hardiness and adaptability to various climatic conditions.

This breed is known for its good egg production capacity, making it a viable option for small-scale poultry farming.

The government also encourages beneficiaries to form self-help groups to facilitate collective marketing of their produce.

This collective approach can help in better pricing and market access for the beneficiaries.

The subsidy scheme is expected to contribute to the nutritional security of the families involved by providing them with a source of protein through eggs.

Moreover, it is anticipated that the scheme will create employment opportunities not only for the beneficiaries but also for others in the community.

The government has also emphasized the importance of sustainable farming practices in poultry farming.

Beneficiaries are encouraged to adopt organic farming methods to ensure the health of the birds and the environment.

The scheme is aligned with the government’s vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

It is also part of the broader efforts to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations.

The implementation of this scheme is monitored regularly to ensure that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme and address any challenges faced during implementation.

The government has allocated a specific budget for this scheme to ensure its sustainability and effectiveness.

In conclusion, the Subsidy Scheme on Establishment of 25 R.I.R. Birds’ Unit for Scheduled Caste is a significant initiative aimed at empowering marginalized communities through sustainable livelihood opportunities in poultry farming.
